summary: Mutual NDA on Halyard paper where the counterparty broadened the Purpose and use right, narrowed the carve-outs, added a 24-month non-solicit, and commented asking for an 18-month tail and Dutch law.

findings.quote: potential commercial opportunities, strategic evaluations, advisory engagements, and any other internal or external business activities of the respective Parties from time to time
findings.why: The Purpose is widened to open-ended business activities rather than discussions about a potential commercial relationship between the parties.
findings.draft_redline: (A) The Parties wish to enter into discussions regarding a potential commercial relationship between them (the Purpose).
findings.note_to_counterparty: We need to keep the Purpose tied to discussions about a potential commercial relationship between us. Open-ended business activities are too broad for a use restriction.

findings.quote: or for its internal business assessment, service benchmarking and market evaluation
findings.why: The insertion permits use for the Receiving Party's own business purposes beyond the Purpose and deletes 'solely'.
findings.draft_redline: not use or exploit the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in any way except solely for the Purpose;
findings.note_to_counterparty: We cannot agree to use for internal assessment, benchmarking or market evaluation. Use must be solely for the Purpose.

findings.quote: [[INS: contemporaneous documentary]] evidence
findings.why: The evidence standard is narrowed from 'written records or other reasonable evidence' to contemporaneous documentary evidence, which is not one of the accepted standards.
findings.draft_redline: which the Receiving Party can demonstrate by written records or other reasonable evidence:
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like to keep the evidence standard as written records or other reasonable evidence, which is workable for both sides.

findings.quote: as evidenced by the Receiving Party's written records dated prior to the date of this Agreement
findings.why: The 'already lawfully held' carve-out remains and relies on written records, which the playbook accepts as an evidence standard.

findings.quote: 3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.why: The independent development carve-out is deleted entirely, leaving only three of the four required exceptions.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Independent development is a standard exception that protects both parties, so we need to reinstate it.

findings.quote: neither Party shall, and each Party shall procure that no member of its Group shall, without the prior written consent of the other Party, directly or indirectly solicit, entice away, offer employment to, engage or employ any Key Personnel
findings.why: A non-solicit running for the term plus 24 months, covering all Key Personnel (including consultants and senior employees) and Groups, with no general-advertising exception and no limit to staff met in the discussions, exceeds the 12-month fallback.
findings.draft_redline: Delete clause 1.1.9 and clause 10.4 in their entirety.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We do not include non-solicitation provisions in our NDAs and cannot accept a 24-month restriction of this breadth. We would be happy to discuss whether a narrower arrangement is needed.

findings.quote: nothing in this Agreement shall operate or be construed so as to exclude, restrict or limit the liability of either Party in respect of fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation
findings.why: The rewording is wordy but the reliance disclaimer is the same in substance and the fraud carve-out is preserved.
findings.fallback_cited: Mutual disclaimers in any reasonable wording.

findings.quote: Our internal policy caps post-termination confidentiality obligations at 18 months from the date of disclosure. Please confirm if Clause 10.3 can be amended accordingly.
findings.why: The counterparty asks for survival of 18 months, below the 2-year minimum Halyard can accept, so this must be escalated; the clause text itself (3 years plus Trade Secrets) matches the playbook.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Thank you for the comment. We can look at a shorter tail but need a minimum of two years post-termination, with Trade Secrets protected for as long as they remain Trade Secrets.

findings.quote: our standard position is for Dutch law and the District Court of Amsterdam (Rechtbank Amsterdam) to apply under Clauses 12.10 and 12.11
findings.why: The counterparty asks to change governing law and courts to Dutch law and Amsterdam, which the playbook does not accept; the clause text itself is England and Wales law and exclusive English jurisdiction.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are not able to move to Dutch law and the Amsterdam courts. We can offer English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales if that helps.

findings.quote: the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction
findings.why: Exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales is the preferred position.

findings.quote: Disclosing Party means the Party that discloses, or procures the disclosure of, Confidential Information to the other Party
findings.why: Disclosing and Receiving Party are defined so either party can be either and the obligations apply equally.

findings.quote: which is either marked or identified as confidential at the time of disclosure or would reasonably be considered confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of its disclosure
findings.why: Definition covers marked or reasonably confidential information disclosed for the Purpose and includes derived notes and analyses.

findings.quote: may disclose the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information to those of its Representatives and members of its Group who strictly need to know
findings.why: Disclosure to Representatives and Group on a need-to-know basis with the Receiving Party liable for them.

findings.quote: to the extent that it is legally permitted to do so
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted, notice is qualified by legal permission, and resisting disclosure is at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: within ten Business Days of receipt of such request
findings.why: Ten Business Days, officer-signed confirmation, and a backup and legal-retention exception with retained copies staying confidential.

findings.quote: shall remain the exclusive property of the Disclosing Party
findings.why: Confidential Information and IP stay with the Disclosing Party and the only licence is use solely for the Purpose.

findings.quote: Neither Party shall make, or permit any person to make, any public announcement
findings.why: Mutual publicity restriction requiring prior written consent, except as required by law.

findings.quote: that Party shall not disclose such personal data unless and until the Parties have agreed and entered into a separate written data processing agreement or data sharing agreement
findings.why: Only business contact details are anticipated and any other personal data needs a separate DPA first; the added EU GDPR reference in 1.1.3 is consistent.

findings.quote: for a period of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: Two-year term with 30 days' notice, and survival of three years with Trade Secrets protected while they remain Trade Secrets.

findings.quote: a Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief
findings.why: Mutual right to seek equitable relief and remedies are cumulative.

findings.quote: without the prior written consent of the other Party
findings.why: No assignment by either party without prior written consent.

findings.quote: not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to derive the composition, source code or underlying structure
findings.why: Reverse engineering of software and prototypes is prohibited.
